fields.Origin: Formed inside Boogie for unknown reasons
fields.Overview (Player): A tiny model spelljamming ship that formed inside Boogie for reasons he cannot explain, half of it inexplicably missing. It is the same model as the personal miniature ship stolen from the instructor Saerthe — a connection Boogie has kept to himself.

bullets: Boogie pulled a tiny model spelljamming ship from his own chest, the same kind he guided in training, except half of it is missing
He has no explanation for how it formed inside him or why it is incomplete
Boogie set it on the table for the crew; Tumak remarked that things had been going missing all over the academy
Revealed to be the same model as the miniature spelljamming ship stolen from Saerthe

fields.Overview (Player): A shirt Casey stole from Mirt's wardrobe and etched with the unfamiliar constellations he glimpsed inside it. It now sits hidden in Tumak's curtained bunk corner.

bullets: Casey stole a shirt from Mirt's wardrobe and etched into it the constellation pattern he saw beyond
Passed to Tumak's hidden bunk corner without explanation, and hidden without question

fields.Overview (Player): A crimson bag of holding, along with valuables, that Tumak claimed for himself from inside Mirt's impossible wardrobe.

bullets: Tumak found and claimed a crimson bag of holding and valuables within Mirt's wardrobe
Holds the containment engine, hidden from Ostekk-10 while Tumak lied to it

fields.Origin: Gifted to Mirt by the spellcaster Zerathis
fields.Overview (Player): Mirt's wardrobe is an impossible object that opens onto a bounded stretch of astral night rather than ordinary space, a magical replica of a place beyond H’catha in the Viren star system, gifted to Mirt by the spellcaster Zerathis.

bullets: A wardrobe in Mirt's chambers whose interior opens onto a bounded stretch of astral night, a floor you can stand on and stars where walls should be
Casey saw unfamiliar constellations and a flickering point inside, and a familiar voice told him 'Go there'
Revealed by Mirt to be a magical replica of a place beyond H’catha in the Viren star system, gifted by the spellcaster Zerathis

fields.Origin: Delivered to Mirt in a crate from the sky dock
fields.Overview (Player): A worm-like centipede creature, one of several that burst from the crate delivered to Mirt, kept alive and sealed back in the crate by Sol as potential evidence in the academy's spreading thefts.

bullets: Worm-like centipede creatures burst from the crate delivered to Mirt and attacked the cadets
Sol subdued the final creature alive and forced it back into the crate, sensing it might matter as evidence
Mirt praised the instinct to keep it alive

links.name: The Living Clue in the Crate

fields.Origin: Saerthe Abizjn's personal miniature, missing from the academy
fields.Overview (Player): A personal miniature spelljamming ship belonging to the instructor Saerthe, taken from him in a manner not yet explained. It is the same model as the incomplete ship that formed inside Boogie.

bullets: Saerthe's own named miniature spelljamming ship, stolen from him in some manner not yet explained
He briefly lost his composure over its theft during the cadets' helm exercise
The same model as the half-missing ship that came out of Boogie's chest

fields.Origin: Jammed into the wall of the simulation chamber during the salvage exercise
fields.Overview (Player): A sigil-engraved metal rod Gregory pulled from the wall of the wrecked simulation chamber — a device built to feed on ambient magic and detonate, now spent. It bears the marking 'Vocath,' and Saerthe has taken it to study.

bullets: Gregory pried it from the wall of the wrecked simulation chamber, a length of sigil-engraved metal that arced energy as it came loose
Built to feed on ambient magical energy and hold the charge until it could no longer contain it — arcane dynamite
Assessed as spent and unlikely to detonate again, save near another strong source of magic
Bears the marking 'Vocath'; Saerthe took it and drew it back before Boogie could examine it
Saerthe produced an illusion of it for Mirt at the bridge

name: Marked Crate at the Sky Dock

fields.Origin: Placed at the Sky Dock by an unknown party
fields.Overview (Player): A crate the crew found at the Sky Dock, tucked behind others and marked with the same symbol as the Vocath rod. Something fills it, though nothing living, and it sat unclaimed while the crew watched.

bullets: A crate Boogie found tucked behind others at the Sky Dock, marked with the same symbol as the Vocath rod
Knocking on it revealed nothing living inside, but it was not hollow
Its contents would route through Mr. Blip, with Toril and H’catha as destinations; no one came for it while the crew watched

fields.Origin: Manifested by Tumak, drawn through a small portal tied to home
fields.Overview (Player): A spectral blade Tumak manifests through a small portal at his call. When he first drew it, his half-runes flared and he felt a tether running toward the home he seeks — the portal itself a piece of that somewhere.

bullets: Summoned by Tumak for the first time in the tyrant-ship shaft fight, a spectral blade drawn out of a small portal
As it left him, his two half-runes flared, and he felt for the first time a tether toward home — the portal a piece of that somewhere
Thrown wide, it curved true and struck the last wisp as the Runekeeper said all things find their way home
Called up a second time against the behir: one blade flickered loose, the other sank in and drove a pulse of force into it

links.name: Tumak's Runes and the Tether Home

fields.Origin: Recovered from a derelict in the salvage simulation
fields.Overview (Player): The logbook the crews raced for in the salvage exercise, found behind the body of something long decomposed. Boogie slipped it into his own chest and has carried it since. Casey and Gregory each bound a duplicate of its pages during the githyanki attack, so three identical copies exist.

bullets: Found in the captain’s quarters of the derelict, half-tucked behind a long-decomposed body
Boogie slipped it inside his own chest without explaining the impulse
Casey bound a duplicate of the pages and Gregory followed with a second, leaving three identical logbooks
Boogie confirmed it still rests in his chest beside the half-ship

fields.Overview (Player): The tyrant ship’s own cargo record. It is what gave the broken autognome in the hold a name — Ostekk-6 — and it lists what else the vessel was carrying.

bullets: Gave the broken autognome in the cargo hold its name: Ostekk-6

fields.Origin: Built by Ostekk; recovered from Vaelorix's body on the Command Deck
fields.Overview (Player): A small iron lamp six or eight inches tall, with a handle and an iris shutter over a faint green light. Ostekk-6 knows it as the containment engine, fourth series, built by Ostekk and kept and studied by Vaelorix, who called it the Lantern of Flourishing. It holds three charges that renew each day, and each one mends a body, constructs better than the living. Ostekk-10 was sent to bring it back.

bullets: Found by Gregory's pull beneath the roots, between two of the dead beholder's eyestalks
Read with a spell: three charges a day, each mending a body, constructs better than the living
A charge spent on Ostekk-6 set his body rebuilding below the waist
Hidden in Tumak's bag of holding while Tumak told Ostekk-10 nothing had been found

fields.Origin: Vaelorix's garden aboard the tyrant ship
fields.Overview (Player): A newly bloomed flower Bartholomew found in Vaelorix's garden. Its scent was familiar and he could not place it. When he breathed it in, his body wanted to become something he had never been, but the flower had already given off most of what it had. He sealed it in one of the garden's containers.

bullets: Found newly bloomed in Vaelorix's garden by Bartholomew
Breathed in, it made his body want to change into something he had never been, and it was not enough
Sealed in one of the garden's containers and kept

fields.Overview (Player): A sending stone Miken carries. Bartholomew caught him speaking into it in the night aboard the tyrant ship. Miken says he was saying hello to his family. Who is at the other end, the crew cannot say.

bullets: Seen by Bartholomew in Miken's hand on the first watch, Miken speaking into it
Miken said he was saying hello to his family
